description: Astro Techies is a group of space technology enthusiasts interested in astronomy, space exploration, and advanced technologies. It focuses on learning about the universe, discovering new innovations, and understanding the technologies used in space missions.
summary:
Echoes of Exploration is an interactive website that tells the stories behind the equipment humanity has sent to the Moon and Mars. Instead of listing technical specifications, it lets visitors explore each piece of hardware as a character in the story of exploration. Equipment cards for Apollo lunar modules, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, ALSEP, Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity, and Ingenuity each open a story popup. These popups cover why the machine was built, what it faced, and what it achieved. All stories are drawn from NASA's own published material and use NASA imagery and our own visuals.

The project makes space history approachable for students and the general public, and shows how each mission built on the one before it. It is built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and hosted on GitHub Pages, so anyone can open it in a browser without installing anything.
details:
What it does and how it works
Echoes of Exploration is a website that presents the Moon and Mars equipment humanity has sent into space as stories. Visitors browse equipment cards divided into Moon and Mars sections. These include the Apollo lunar modules, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, ALSEP, Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity, and Ingenuity. Clicking a card opens a popup that tells the story of that machine: why it was built, the challenges it faced, and what it achieved.

Benefits and intended impact
The site makes space exploration history easy to understand for students and the general public. Presenting each machine as a story, instead of a list of specifications, helps people connect with the missions. It also shows how each generation of equipment built on the work of the one before it.

Tools and technologies

  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with no frameworks
  • Mission data stored in a separate JavaScript data file, so new equipment can be added without changing the page code
  • Content sourced from NASA's official mission pages
  • Images from the NASA Image and Video Library, plus our own visuals for the lunar rover, Spirit and Opportunity, and Ingenuity
  • Version control with Git, hosted on GitHub Pages so it works in any browser

Creativity
The creative idea is to treat the equipment as characters, so each machine's "echo" of exploration is heard through its own story. The card-and-popup layout keeps the page clean while letting visitors choose how deep to go.

Factors we considered

  • Accuracy: all facts come from NASA sources
  • Accessibility: the site is lightweight, works on any device, and needs no installation
  • Scalability: the data-driven structure lets us add more missions later
  • Clarity: the stories use simple language so non-experts can follow them
